label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 3 pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation

report.summary: No delay observed in the window: transfers were fast, the outbox kept up, and all 476 deliveries succeeded in about 72 ms. Late notifications are not reproduced here.

findings.claim: Outbox is keeping up: pending is 1-4 and oldest undelivered age is at most ~1.06 s; there are no failures.
findings.reason: Arrivals 480 vs publications 476 (difference 4, settled); failed gauge stayed 0; oldest undelivered age max 1.06 s.

findings.claim: All deliveries succeeded on attempt 1 with low latency (p95 ~77 ms), mostly consumer auth time; no retries, auth, server or network errors.
findings.reason: 476 of 476 SUCCESS, total p50 72 ms, max 96 ms; the log shows 0 errors of any type.

findings.claim: The transfer API is healthy: no server errors and p99 latency ~0.25 s.

limitations: Window is only about 150 s, so intermittent or load-dependent delays may not appear.
Delivery log listing shows only the earliest 20 of 476 records; the pending gauge is sampled only 5 times.
next_checks: Re-run the checks over a window when customers actually reported late notifications.
Inspect the downstream notification pipeline timings after consumer receipt.

alternatives.reason: Only delivery to the consumer was measured, not what happens after it.
alternatives.hypothesis: Delay occurs downstream of LedgerCore (external consumer or notification provider processing after receipt).

alternatives.reason: The window shows steady 32 per 10 s arrivals and no backlog, so any incident would have to be at another time.
alternatives.hypothesis: The delay happened outside this 150 s window, for example a transient burst or outage.

A.rule: no failed deliveries and pending stayed low

report.summary: In this window, transfer notifications were not observed to be late. The outbox backlog stayed small (max 4 pending, oldest age at most 1.06 s) and all 476 deliveries succeeded in about 72 ms.

findings.claim: The outbox kept pace with arrivals. The backlog was at most 4 pending, with the oldest undelivered item at most 1.06 s old and none failed.
findings.reason: 480 arrivals vs 476 publications over 150 s; pending 1-4, failed 0, oldest age max 1.06 s.

findings.claim: All 476 delivery attempts succeeded on the first try, with no auth, network or server errors.
findings.reason: The outcome counts cover all 476 records: success 476, every error category 0, and all at attempt 1.

findings.claim: Delivery latency was low (p95 77 ms). Consumer auth accounted for most of it, and the consumer handler was negligible.
findings.reason: Total p50 72 ms, p95 77 ms, max 96 ms; consumer auth p50 70.6 ms; handler p50 0.023 ms.

findings.claim: The transfers API was healthy: no server errors, p99 about 0.25 s.

alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness occurs outside this 150 s window, or downstream of the consumer (push or SMS provider, device delivery).
alternatives.reason: Only the LedgerCore-to-consumer hop was measured, and only for this short window.

alternatives.hypothesis: A transient backlog caused the delays.
alternatives.reason: The peak pending count was 4 and the oldest age about 1 s, too small to explain customer-visible lateness.

limitations: The window is only 150 s, and the final 10 s bucket shows 0 arrivals and 0 publications.
Only the earliest 100 of 476 delivery records were listed, and nothing downstream of the consumer was observed.
next_checks: Re-check over a longer window that covers the times customers reported late notifications.
Inspect downstream notification provider latency and end-to-end timestamps from transfer commit to customer receipt.
